classification.difficultyReason: Convert mixed length units and use equal opposite sides before adding the four boundary lengths.

content.prompt: Calculate the perimeter of these shapes. Give your answer in the smaller unit.

spec.description: Rectangle tilted clockwise, with its long edges descending towards the right. The upper long edge is labelled 8 cm and the right short edge is labelled 30 mm. Four open right-angle marks are retained. Opposite long sides have double ticks and opposite short sides have single ticks.
spec.mathematics: Opposite sides of the rectangle are equal; adjacent sides are unequal. Convert 8 cm to 80 mm and add all four sides.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given dimensions and structural marks are visible; the perimeter is held in the answer.

spec.description: Narrow rectangle with its long axis descending from upper left to lower right. The upper-left short edge is labelled 40 cm and the lower-left long edge is labelled 1.2 m. Four open right-angle marks are retained. Opposite long sides have double ticks and opposite short sides have single ticks.
spec.mathematics: Convert 1.2 m to 120 cm and add two long sides and two short sides.
spec.answerVisibility: Given dimensions and structural marks are visible; the supplied perimeter is held in the answer.

spec.description: Horizontal rectangle with 90 cm above its top edge and 0.3 m beside its right edge. Four open right-angle marks and matching single ticks on the vertical sides are retained.
spec.mathematics: Convert 0.3 m to 30 cm and add all four sides.
